active_paradigms.idea: Symmetry-reduced parametric families searched globally with scipy.optimize.differential_evolution
active_paradigms.description: Instead of optimizing 42 free coordinates, restrict to highly symmetric ansatz families known to contain near-optimal 14-point configurations: (a) 7 antipodal pairs parametrized by 7 unit vectors with antipodal symmetry; (b) a twisted double heptagon (two parallel regular 7-gons with twist angle, radius, and separation as the only 3 parameters); (c) icosahedron + 2 points placed with tetrahedral symmetry. For each family, run scipy.optimize.differential_evolution on the few remaining free parameters (3–15 dims) with the exact objective (dmin/dmax)^2 computed directly from the parametrization. Differential evolution is a true global optimizer over the small parameter space, escaping the local optima that plague SLSQP in 42 dimensions. Because each evaluation is cheap (one 91-pair distance computation), allow large populations (popsize 40–100) and thousands of generations within the timeout. Take the best family result and finish with the existing SLSQP t-reformulation only as a final KKT polish.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary score (dmin/dmax)^2 by escaping 42-dimensional local optima via low-dimensional global search over symmetric configurations.
active_paradigms.cautions: Verify each parametrization actually yields 14 distinct points; antipodal-pair families fix dmax to be a diameter only if points lie on a sphere — check whether dmax might be exceeded by other pairs. Keep differential_evolution workers=1 or fixed seed for reproducibility. Do not over-restrict: include at least 3–4 distinct families so the global search spans genuinely different topologies.

active_paradigms.idea: Basin-hopping global search directly on the ratio objective with spherical projection
active_paradigms.description: Replace the gradient-ascent-then-polish pipeline with scipy.optimize.basinhopping, a Monte-Carlo global optimizer with built-in local minimization. Define the objective as -(dmin/dmax)^2 with all points kept on the unit sphere by projection after every step (dmax on the sphere is then bounded by the diameter 2, giving a clean objective). Use the BFGS or L-BFGS-B local minimizer on the 42 coordinates (42 minus 3 rotation + scaling degrees of freedom), with a soft-min surrogate smoothed enough for usable gradients (e.g., log-sum-exp of 1/d). Set niter to several hundred with temperature tuned to typical objective fluctuation, and run 5–10 independent basins from structured seeds (icosahedral, heptagonal, antipodal). Acceptance on the exact hard ratio, tracking the best ever seen. This is a genuinely different global mechanism from both the current multi-start gradient ascent and the SLSQP basin hopping around a single point.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary score by exploring a much wider set of basins than the current perturb-around-best strategy, which locks onto one topology.
active_paradigms.cautions: The hard min is non-smooth; the local minimizer must use a smoothed objective or it will stall immediately. Keep the exact (hard) ratio as the acceptance/tracking criterion, not the smoothed one. Fix random seeds via numpy Generator passed through the basin-hopping interval class or seed argument for reproducibility. Watch runtime: cap niter so total work fits the timeout.

active_paradigms.idea: Contact-graph enumeration: solve candidate triangulation systems as nonlinear equations with scipy.optimize.root
active_paradigms.description: At an optimum of (dmin/dmax)^2, many pairwise distances are exactly equal to dmin (the 'contact graph'), and typically several equal dmax. Exploit this structure: enumerate plausible contact-graph topologies consistent with n=14 in 3D (graphs with degrees 4–6 per vertex, near-triangulated, ~30–35 contact edges, plus 1–3 diameter pairs). For each candidate graph, set up the system: squared distances of contact edges equal a common value t, squared distances of diameter pairs equal a common value D, remaining edges >= t. Solve the polynomial system with scipy.optimize.root (hybr/lm method) from randomized starting points; each converged solution with all inequality constraints satisfied is a stationary candidate, and evaluate the exact ratio on it. Use graph-symmetry pruning (vertex-transitive or dihedral symmetry classes) to keep the enumeration tractable. This attacks the problem through its KKT/contact structure rather than generic continuous optimization, potentially reaching exact optimal configurations with many active constraints that generic optimizers only approximate.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary score by constructing configurations where the number of active min-distance and max-distance constraints is maximal, which is the signature of true optima.
active_paradigms.cautions: The nonlinear system is over/under-determined depending on graph choice — count equations (contacts + diameters + gauge fixing) against 42 unknowns and only attempt graphs where the count is feasible (use least-squares root method 'lm' otherwise). Randomized starts for each graph; discard solutions violating inactive-edge inequalities. Runtime control: cap enumeration to a few hundred graphs with a per-graph iteration limit, deterministic ordering and seeds.

tried_paradigms.idea: Direct constrained NLP via scipy.optimize.minimize (SLSQP) on the reformulated problem: maximize t subject to d(i,j)^2 >= t and d(i,j)^2 <= 1
tried_paradigms.description: The evaluator hints the exact reformulation: introduce auxiliary variable t and solve max t with 91 lower-bound constraints d(i,j)^2 >= t and 91 upper-bound constraints d(i,j)^2 <= 1 over 42+1 variables. Implement as scipy.optimize.minimize with method='SLSQP' minimizing -t, passing all constraints as a single vectorized inequality function returning np.concatenate([d2 - t, 1 - d2]). Use analytic gradients: for constraint d(i,j)^2, gradient wrt point i is 2(xi-xj). Run from many seeds (the current best configuration plus icosahedron-based and random starts), and take the best feasible result. SLSQP handles this smooth problem well and converges to KKT points of the true ratio objective, unlike soft-min gradient heuristics which stall near saddle regions. Finally rescale so dmax=1.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: primary combined_score (dmin/dmax)^2, converging to the true local/global optimum of the exact ratio
tried_paradigms.cautions: Scale points so dmax is near 1 before optimization; provide the Jacobian of the constraint vector (sparse-like dense array) for speed and reliability; check feasibility after solve and fall back to best seed if SLSQP fails; keep number of restarts modest to fit timeout.

tried_paradigms.idea: Max-min distance geometry via SDP-like relaxation using scipy: optimize Gram matrix with fixed diameter graph structure (bipartite/antipodal ansatz)
tried_paradigms.description: Exploit the known structure of good 14-point solutions: the optimal configuration likely has dmax realized by few antipodal-like pairs. Parametrize the configuration as 7 near-antipodal pairs (points ±vi plus small radial perturbations), reducing dimensionality. Then maximize the minimum of the 91 distances using a smooth exact reformulation: minimize sum of exp(-d^2/temperature) via scipy.optimize.minimize (method='L-BFGS-B' or 'trust-constr') over the ~21 pair-direction parameters plus per-point radii. This drastically reduces the search space and directly encodes that dmax is a diameter. Multiple random initial pair directions (e.g., from icosahedron axes, Thomson-like solutions) give diverse basins.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: primary score by exploiting structural ansatz that dmax pairs are diameters, reducing a 42-dim problem to ~28-dim structured one
tried_paradigms.cautions: Verify the antipodal assumption actually holds for the best found solutions; allow free-space fallback where pairs are not exactly antipodal; use enough random restarts (30+) with fixed seeds; normalize final points so dmax=1.

tried_paradigms.idea: Simulated annealing / basin-hopping global search with scipy.optimize.basinhopping on the exact ratio objective
tried_paradigms.description: Use scipy.optimize.basinhopping with a custom acceptance test on the objective -(dmin/dmax)^2 (with inner local minimizer SLSQP or L-BFGS-B on a smooth surrogate like -softmin(d^2)/softmax(d^2)). This combines global stochastic exploration with strong local convergence, escaping the local optima that trap the current projected-gradient pipeline. Seed from the current best configuration plus icosahedron-based starts. Run ~200 hopping iterations with adaptive step size targeting ~50% acceptance; each inner minimization runs only ~50 iterations to keep total time in budget. Track the best-ever configuration and return it normalized.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: primary score by escaping local maxima of the nonconvex ratio landscape; consistency of the final score
tried_paradigms.cautions: The raw ratio objective is nondifferentiable at ties; use a temperature-softened surrogate (log-sum-exp of -d^2 and +d^2) for the inner minimizer but evaluate true ratio for acceptance. Bound total runtime: pre-time a single inner minimize and scale iteration counts. Use fixed seed via numpy Generator passed through the take_step callback.
